sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Gi signaling activity of the FLAG-tagged S1PR5 construct was measured by cAMP assay and found to be similar to wild-type S1PRs (L5).
sites.rationale: S1PR5 is a GPCR with residues 1–39 forming the extracellular N-terminal domain (topology landmarks). The ledger (L1, L4) documents a full-length, membrane-anchored construct with an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by a FLAG tag prepended to the native sequence; after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG is displayed on the extracellular face before native M1. No paper names a specific residue junction, so the position is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=0 (prepend). L5 confirms that this tagged construct retains Gi signaling activity comparable to wild-type, qualifying as surface_and_function. Full-length human S1PR5 was engineered with an added HA signal peptide, FLAG-tag, and Ala-Gly-Arg-Ala linker at the N-terminus for expression in insect cells (L1/L4). The native S1PR5 has no signal peptide (topology: residues 1–39 extracellular); the HA signal peptide was added exogenously to drive secretory trafficking, placing the FLAG tag on the extracellular face after HA-SP cleavage, immediately before the native M1. No specific residue junction within the N-terminal extracellular span is named; the extracellular N-terminus is the only surface terminus available on a GPCR.

sources.claim: Similar to wild-type S1PRs, the modified versions exhibited Gi signaling activity (Supplementary information, Fig.

literature_notes: L1 and L4 describe the same N-terminal FLAG construct (HA signal peptide + FLAG + AGRA linker prepended to full-length S1PR5); L5 validates its Gi signaling function. L2 describes the same N-terminal FLAG arrangement plus a BRIL domain fused into ICL3 (A223–R241) and a C-terminal His-tag; the ICL3 and C-terminal positions are intracellular and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any insertion in ECL1 (96–108), ECL2 (174–191), or ECL3 (274–287). The position is topology_derived because no paper specifies which residue of the N-terminal extracellular span carries the junction — the HA signal peptide is exogenous and its cleavage site within the added construct is not stated relative to canonical UniProt numbering.

literature_other_positions.note: BRIL (apocytochrome b562RIL) was inserted between A223 and R241 in ICL3 of full-length S1PR5 to stabilize the receptor for crystallization; ICL3 spans residues 214–252 (intracellular), so this is not a surface tag site.
R241 is the C-terminal boundary of the BRIL insertion in ICL3 (intracellular 214–252); recorded as the second named junction of the same intracellular domain-insertion event.

A PreScission Protease site and decahistidine tag were added at the C-terminus of the S1PR5 crystallization construct; the C-terminus falls within the intracellular region (309–398) and is not a surface tag site.
